Kara — great to meet the team today, and thanks for the artifacts. Quick read-through looks fine; we noted the PII guidance in the PDF. Below is a practical bench plan and the minimal data/access we’ll need to start.

Proposed bench objective (2-week window):
- Baseline model fit for factual QA over your prioritized query set (120 queries).
- Grounding health: precision@1/3, grounding rate, citation accuracy, and hallucination rate on a 30-query focused subset.
- Latency/cost benchmarking for throughput targets you mentioned (90th pct latency target = 300ms per token).

Initial recommended configurations (tradeoffs):
1) Fast / cost-efficient: redwood-opt-6.8b-quant (compile-time optimizations, lower VRAM)
   - Expect: lower latency, lower factual depth on long-context, good for short Q/A.
2) Balanced: redwood-opt-13b (fp16)
   - Expect: better factuality and answer completeness for multi-hop clinical queries.
3) High-fidelity: redwood-opt-70b (low-precision quantized variant for bench)
   - Expect: best grounding and fewer ambiguous responses; higher cost.

Embeddings / retrieval:
- Recommend: text-embed-ada-2 (dense) as baseline; run a hybrid experiment with BM25 (Elastic + FAISS hybrid) for recall-sensitive queries.
- Chunking: 250–400 token chunks with 20% overlap for clinical notes (preserve section headers).
- Retriever recall probes: recall@10 on a held-out set and retroactive proximity checks for citation accuracy.

Reranker options:
- Lightweight cross-encoder reranker (fine-tune on your labeled pairs, 2–4 epoch run) as primary.
- Fallback: off-the-shelf lexical re-ranker + passage scoring for throughput-critical paths.

Evaluations / metrics we will provide:
- Precision@1/3/5, recall@k, MRR, grounding rate (percentage of answers with correct source citation), hallucination rate (false factual statements per 100 responses), latency distribution, tokens/cost estimates.

Deliverables we’ll provide by kickoff:
- redwood_rag_bench_plan.pdf (high-level test matrix + runbook) [attached]
- clarion_prompt_suite_v1.jsonl (starter prompt set + safety flags) [attached]
- Links to eval workbook and expected column formats.

What we need from you before Wed EOD:
- S3 or Drive link with a 500–1,000 doc sample (de-identified where possible).
- Confirmation on priority query subset (if you want different weighting for regulatory vs clinical).
- Any redlines on PII policy (we flagged a couple of fields that should not be indexed).

If that timeline looks OK we’ll schedule a short kickoff on May 24 to confirm access and initial run parameters.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: RAG bench inputs you requested

Kara / team — quick technical addendum to Grace’s plan with concrete hyperparams we’ll run for the bench. I’m including reasons so you can prioritize which runs matter most.

Quoted from Grace’s message: 
> Chunking: 250–400 token chunks with 20% overlap for clinical notes (preserve section headers).

Agreed — we will run a chunking sweep: 200 / 300 / 400 tokens with 10/20/30% overlap. For each chunk size we’ll measure recall and citation-span correctness.

Retriever hyperparams (initial):
- Dense ANN: FAISS HNSW index (efSearch=64 default), nprobe equivalent ~16 when using IVF; k candidates = 50.
- Hybrid: Elastic BM25 (top 100) merged with FAISS top 100, dedupe by passage id.
- Similarity thresholds: cosine >= 0.72 as a conservative keep for clinical snippets; we’ll log distribution so you can tune.

Reranker experiments:
- Cross-encoder (small transformer, ~80M params) fine-tuned for binary relevance on 1k labeled pairs (if available) — expected lift in precision@1 of 8–12 pts vs lexical.
- Learned logistic scorer (features: BM25 score, token overlap, embedding cosine) as a low-cost alternative.

Grounding metrics / probes we’ll compute (examples):
- Citation accuracy: exact-match of claim span to source doc + contextual confidence score.
- Hallucination probe: human-annotated 50-question set where annotators mark unsupported claims; report hallucinations per 100 answers.
- Referential drift: rate at which the model cites unrelated docs (false citation rate).

Model bench plan:
- Run matrix: {models} x {chunk_sizes} x {retriever variants} x {reranker variants}. To keep runs tractable we’ll prioritize: redwood-opt-13b fp16 and redwood-opt-6.8b-quant first, then run 70b if we see material gaps on factuality.

Operational asks for kickoff:
- Access: a read-only S3 path with a sample corpus (500–1,000 docs) and 120 queries as a CSV.
- Optional: 200 labeled relevance pairs if you have any existing click/relevance logs (helps reranker).

I’ll attach a short checklist in the kickoff doc so engineering can hook up credentials quickly. Happy to jump on the May 24 kickoff — propose 10:00am PT.

— Soojin
Senior ML Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference
